Title: Spoofing of Source Data Store SQL Database
Justification: The database is embedded in the same container (no network hop to impersonate). Container isolation is covered separately (manual threat M2).

Title: Cross Site Scripting
Justification: Juice Shop is built with known XSS flaws (e.g. search and feedback). Untrusted input echoed back to the browser could run script and steal a session token. To confirm by testing the search box and feedback form on my own instance.

Title: Persistent Cross Site Scripting
Justification: Stored input (reviews, feedback, profile fields) is shown to other users, so one injection can hit every visitor. To confirm by saving a harmless test payload and viewing it from a second account.

Title: Weak Access Control for a Resource
Justification: Broken access control is number 1 in the OWASP Top 10. Test whether one user can read another user's basket or orders by changing IDs in requests, and whether admin-only pages open without admin rights.

Title: Spoofing of Destination Data Store SQL Database
Justification: Duplicate of threat 10, analysed there.

Title: Potential SQL Injection Vulnerability for SQL Database
Justification: Login and product search are known to be injectable in Juice Shop, risking authentication bypass and data extraction. Plan: test the login form with a crafted email value and the search endpoint with injection strings.

Title: Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Web Application(Node.js) or SQL Database
Justification: No rate limiting is expected, so repeated heavy requests could slow or stall the Node process. Impact is limited to availability of a lab target. Test only with a small, controlled burst against my own instance.

Title: Spoofing of the Human User External Destination Entity
Justification: Duplicate of threat 39, analysed there.

Title: External Entity Human User Potentially Denies Receiving Data
Justification: A browser denying receipt of a page has no security impact for this app; accountability is assessed under threats 41 and 87.

Title: Data Flow HTTP response Is Potentially Interrupted
Justification: A network interruption has little impact on a single-user lab target; availability is assessed under threat 16.

Title: Spoofing the Azure Firewall Process
Justification: Out of scope. Azure Firewall (NSG) internals are managed by Microsoft under the shared responsibility model; I assess my own rule configuration instead (threats 49 and 95).

Title: Spoofing the Human User External Entity
Justification: A user could be impersonated by forging or stealing the login token (JWT); Juice Shop has known weak token handling. Test by decoding my own token and checking whether a modified one is accepted.

Title: Potential Lack of Input Validation for Azure Firewall
Justification: Firewall-side validation is Azure-managed; input validation in the application itself is assessed under threat 84.

Title: Potential Data Repudiation by Azure Firewall
Justification: By default the NSG does not record who connected, so a connection attempt could not be proven afterwards. To check: whether any NSG/VNet flow logging or VM authentication logging is enabled.

Title: Data Flow Sniffing
Justification: The shop is served over plain HTTP, so passwords and session tokens cross the network unencrypted. The NSG limits who can connect, not who can observe the path. Confirm with a packet capture and by checking there is no HTTPS redirect.
